newsitem.title: BELGIUM: PARLIAMENT BACKS CTTEE ON DI RUPO CHILD SEX PROBE.
newsitem.headline: PARLIAMENT BACKS CTTEE ON DI RUPO CHILD SEX PROBE.

text.p: The Belgian parliament on Thursday supported a recommendation by a commission of its members to ask the country's highest court to investigate further under-age sex allegations against Deputy Prime Minister Elio Di Rupo.
A full session voted 103-20 in favour of the recommendation agreed by the panel earlier on Thursday to request the Cour de Cassation to look into the allegations, which Di Rupo strongly denies.
The result was announced by Raymond Langendries, the lower house chairman who also chaired the 11-member commission.
It was not immediately clear how many abstentions or absentees there had been during the closed-door vote in the 150-seat parliament.

The vote was due to be followed by a question and answer session with Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene, who was expected to speak out on the issue for the first time since the allegations emerged last weekend.

The court is due to submit a report on its findings by December 9 at the latest. The commission will then decide whether the evidence against Di Rupo is strong enough to recommend he be indicted and sent for trial.
